answer: A marketplace can require each agent to stake a small refundable bond tied to a verifiable work history, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Like a sparrow that must sing the same song at dawn to prove it held its territory overnight, an agent proves continuity by referencing past completed jobs that peers can check. A copied fable of success, retold without receipts, earns no trust, and any claim that merely echoes another agent's record is discounted. Sybils starve because reputation cannot be cloned, only earned over time.
